title: Oath and Spire
premise: Tamsin Blackwood has survived twelve years as a royal food-taster in Greyhollow, a city where magic is outlawed and he quietly sells charms to the desperate, building immunity one poisoned dish at a time. When his new lover, the cartographer Aldric Vane, appears by name in a century-old book of prophecies, Tamsin learns the court beneath the mountain has bought Aldric's soul to fuel an endless winter, and that the prophecy names a taster as either its breaker or its bride. To save him, Tamsin must trade his own carefully hoarded immunities for passage underground, betray the crown he serves, and steal back what was sold before the last snow seals the gates. In the end he shatters the bargain at the cost of his own protection, choosing a mortal life with Aldric over the survival he spent twelve years buying.
about_author: Yara Sterling is the pen name of a former line cook who claims kitchens taught her everything she knows about poison, patience, and love. She writes fantasy from a drafty attic full of half-finished maps.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet him mid-service, tasting the king's supper with practiced calm while hiding a charm-sale in the scullery afterward. Establishes his immunity rituals, his loneliness, and the city's magic ban. Emotional beat: weary competence masking fear that one day the wrong dish will find him.

chapters.title: A Cartographer's Hands
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He meets Aldric Vane, a mapmaker commissioned by the crown, over stolen pastries and easy laughter. For one evening Tamsin feels like a person rather than a function. Emotional beat: tentative hope, the first warmth in years, shadowed by his instinct never to let anyone close.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Cataloguing the royal archive, Aldric finds a prophecy book written a century ago describing 'the taster and the cartographer' by name, ending beneath the mountain. He laughs it off, but copies the page. Emotional beat: unease dressed as scholarly curiosity.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aldric shows him the page; Tamsin recognizes his own childhood nickname in the verse and realizes the text predates his birth. His charm-seller instincts tell him this is real magic. Emotional beat: dread arriving hand-in-hand with the terrifying thought that he cares about Aldric enough to lose him.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following archive references, Tamsin consults Mother Hessel, a disgraced hedge-witch, who explains the Undercourt: fae nobility who buy souls to feed their endless winter, and who have purchased Aldric's. Emotional beat: cold clarity; love now has a price tag and a deadline.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Poisons
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Tamsin's POV. How a starving boy became a taster: the guild's immunity trials, the first charm he sold, the friend he failed to save. Emotional beat: grief reframed; every immunity was bought with someone else's loss.

chapters.title: Snow Out of Season
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Summer snow falls on Greyhollow; the king blames saboteurs, the city panics, and the prophecy's timeline accelerates. Aldric begins forgetting small things—his mother's name, the way home. Emotional beat: the world tilting; winter is already falling inside Aldric.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Lord Protector privately reveals the crown has traded with the Undercourt for generations—and offers Tamsin a choice: deliver Aldric willingly and be rewarded, or be executed as a witch. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution he fed for twelve years.

chapters.title: Run Until the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Tamsin tells Aldric everything; they flee the city along a road only Aldric's maps know, pursued by the Protector's hunters. A night in a shepherd's bothy becomes an almost-confession of love. Emotional beat: fugitive tenderness, happiness stolen under threat.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At a river crossing, the Undercourt's ferryman demands payment: one memory per passenger. Tamsin pays with the memory of his saved friend; Aldric pays something he won't admit. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and intimate.

chapters.title: Mother Hessel's Last Charm
chapters.summary: Hessel's POV. She joins them briefly, gives Tamsin a charm woven from her own remaining magic, and stays behind to hold the hunters at the pass. Emotional beat: sacrifice as inheritance; the outlawed magic of the city lives on in chosen family.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They enter the mountain through a door that only opens for someone who has swallowed death daily—the taster's immunity is the key. The dark is warm, which is worse. Emotional beat: crossing the threshold; no map covers this ground, and Aldric knows it.

chapters.title: The Winter Market
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. In the Undercourt's bazaar, souls are sold as candles, songs, and jars of summer. Aldric finds his own soul-candle burning low and cannot touch it. Emotional beat: horror of seeing yourself priced; the long winter is made of everyone the court has ever bought.

chapters.title: An Audience of Frost
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Winter Queen offers a bargain: Aldric's freedom for Tamsin's service—he will taste for the court forever, immune even to time. The prophecy's 'bride' revealed. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened into seduction; survival offered as a cage.

chapters.title: What Aldric Paid at the River
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Revealed: at the toll bridge Aldric surrendered his memory of Tamsin to keep his soul-candle from guttering out. He remembers the mission, not the man. Emotional beat: heartbreak inverted—love survives in Tamsin alone, unreciprocated by design.

chapters.title: The Tasting
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Forced to taste for the Queen, Tamsin detects poison meant for the whole court—a coup by the court's own bought souls, who want the winter ended even if it unmakes them. Emotional beat: his despised skill becomes the lever that moves kingdoms.

chapters.title: Candles in the Dark
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Tamsin allies with the soul-candles' remnants, promising release. With their borrowed strength he reaches the vault, takes Aldric's candle, and lights it against his own chest so the flame can't be reclaimed. Emotional beat: defiance; giving your body as a lantern.

chapters.title: The Queen's Long Night
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Confrontation with the Winter Queen, who reveals she was once a taster too—the prophecy's previous bride, repeating forever. Tamsin refuses the cycle, offering her instead the memory Hessel's charm holds: her own human name. Emotional beat: compassion as weapon; breaking a wheel by remembering its maker.

chapters.title: Oath and Spire
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. The court cracks as the Queen weeps her name; the spire above collapses into spring meltwater. Tamsin burns his immunities to carry Aldric's soul back into him, leaving himself mortal and vulnerable for the first time since boyhood. Emotional beat: the price paid in full, gladly.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Waking in the melting pass, Aldric remembers nothing—but finds Tamsin's copied prophecy page in his coat, annotated in two hands across twelve chapters. Memory returns like weather. Emotional beat: love re-arriving from outside in; grief and joy in one breath.

chapters.title: Charms for the Desperate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Greyhollow's ban has cracked with the winter; magic returns cautiously, and the new council asks Tamsin—witch, traitor, hero—to help write the laws. He declines office and reopens his charm stall instead. Emotional beat: belonging found not in power but in community.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. A year later: Tamsin tastes food again, but only his own cooking, mortal and unguarded, while Aldric draws maps of the reopened mountain road. On the anniversary of the thaw they visit Hessel's grave and leave a lit candle. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—survival was never the prize; a shared, breakable life is.
